caveats: Expected errors come from the model's own probabilities; the test is only valid if they are calibrated. They are recalibrated per fold on the discovery rows only; grossly wrong probabilities make the check unavailable.
Groups are axis-aligned rules or clusters of similar rows, so an oblique or very small region may be missed or found only in part.
A group is an association found in the evaluation data, not a causal explanation: it says where the model fails, not why.

Features that describe a group may be proxies for sensitive characteristics (for example a relationship status standing in for sex), so the rule can reveal a protected subpopulation even though no sensitive column was named.
Detection power depends on the sample size; no group found does not mean none exists.

Hidden failure group (tree): segment = d AND tenure_years > 6.57 AND income_k > 57 — 34 held-out rows, observed error 76.5% vs 27.0% expected; 6 confirmed group(s) in total.
Hidden failure group policy (configured): consequence 'hold', assessment required. A confirmed group blocks promotion.

Evidence note: these results rely on declared (unverified) producer metadata: training_validity.overfit_gap, training_validity.train_eval_overlap, training_validity.train_duplicate_rows, operational.dependency_match.
Suggested action (behaviour.roc_auc): Improve the model's ranking quality (features, model family).

Suggested action (behaviour.hidden_failure_groups): Investigate the reported group: check its data volume and label quality, add or engineer features that separate it, or retrain with more examples from it.
These suggestions are starting points, not guarantees.
